acceptanceCriteria: The Codex review prompt in the lane common charter and the codex-cli review skill forbid corvint-tasks mutations and name receipt audit as the check.
Decide whether corvint-tasks gains a read-only environment marker; if yes, every mutation refuses with one closed code when it is set and a focused test covers it.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 on queue:corvint:main. The V1-1305 builder ran the one-round Codex review as `codex exec -s read-only ... </dev/null` from its plain clone under /private/tmp. The review nevertheless executed `corvint-tasks ticket attach-evidence` against V1-1305 and the write succeeded: receipt 000000004563.json, request-id v11305-review-invalid-ocm-shape-20261012, actor russelllewis role OWNER, ticket revision 1 -> 2. The Codex sandbox only guards the filesystem of the review cwd; corvint-tasks resolves the journal under the primary checkout .git/taskman and the local-operator actor binding is recorded, not authenticated (decision 0003). Consequence: reviewer-written evidence is indistinguishable from builder or owner evidence, which weakens the reviewer independence the lane protocol relies on, and an unexpected revision bump can make a later expected-revision mutation by the builder refuse STALE_TICKET. Options: (a) the review prompt and skill state that the reviewer must not run corvint-tasks mutations and the orchestrator checks receipt audit for reviewer-attributed writes; (b) corvint-tasks honours an environment marker such as CORVINT_TASKS_READ_ONLY=1 that refuses every mutation with one closed code so a sandboxed reviewer cannot write; (c) attach-evidence records a reviewer role distinct from OWNER. Not a corvint-tasks defect; filed as a protocol gap.
title: Review lanes: a read-only Codex review can still write Tasks journal evidence (attach-evidence on V1-1305)
